scope: Executable follow-ups grounded in PR121979, PR142304 and issue142223; broader research belongs to the user's other model. No new measurements.

common_protocol.preregistration: Before execution, commit hypotheses, exact source/toolchain/feature gates, fixtures, route counters, masks, budgets, repetitions/order and decision thresholds. These proposals are not that frozen preregistration.
stages: Qualify evaluator using positive and deliberately mismatched controls
common_protocol.oracle: Use independently obtained fixture identity and version; preserve raw outputs, strict diffs and path receipts. No sleeping as a synchronization oracle. Keep setup, measured phase and teardown receipts distinct.
common_protocol.ordering: Resource comparisons use separate fresh processes, declared warmup, counterbalanced AB/BA or balanced factorial blocks; report distributions and per-host results.
common_protocol.attempt_accounting: Retain every launch and failed calibration. Setup or evaluator failure means BLOCKED, not an implementation pass/fail.

decisions.KEEP: Registered contract and improvement threshold pass in the measured configuration
decisions.KILL: Registered contract violation or registered harmful resource result
decisions.REVISE: Mixed result or narrower mechanism suggests a revised, separately registered experiment
decisions.BLOCKED: Unqualified evaluator, missing actual route, missing version barrier or missing dependency

common_protocol.limitations: Finite fixtures support bounded claims, not future semantic fidelity. Functional local fixture tests only; no authentication/authorization bypass or token-decision probes.

experiments.title: Real Pod REST / cache / codec differential
experiments.hypothesis: Conversion and benign Get/List results agree on the same stored object version once both caches have observed it; any defaulting difference is explicitly exposed.
experiments.why: Original PR questioned defaulting and future path drift. Completed copy tests use synthetic storage and do not establish real-cache provenance.
harness: Root-repository integration test using real Pod REST storage and the cache decorator, with direct clients and a normal loopback client/informer on the same isolated etcd prefix
pkg/registry/core/pod/storage/storage_test.go:newStorage is a starting point, but its UndecoratedStorage must be replaced for this experiment
test/integration/apiserver/watchcache_test.go and test/integration/framework supply real server/etcd patterns
factors: Get and List, namespace selector cases, managedFields absent/present
Normal supported Pod writes and separately registered codec-level stored fixtures with omitted defaultable fields
Exact UID/resourceVersion synchronized snapshots; no concurrent updates during comparison
controls: Normal fully specified fixture must agree
Known informer managedFields trimming must be detected by raw comparison
Counters prove cache-enabled construction and actual Get/List route; enabling a flag alone is insufficient
observations: Raw HTTP decoded, informer and direct values/errors
Separate GVK and managedFields diffs; never mask defaulted spec/status fields
Cache/backend call counts, storage codec, identity/version and feature-gate receipts
Source ownership snapshots at the conversion boundary and subsequent independent reads
experiments.gate: BLOCKED if paths or same-version barrier cannot be established. REVISE on unexplained representation/defaulting difference. Copy-preservation conclusions require a real cache-owned source oracle, not only a later fresh backend read.
caveats: Generated lister RV=0 may allow older cache data; synchronized comparison is a correctness condition, not proof of stronger freshness
REST Store.Get is not an explicit defaulting hook; locate and record codec/defaulting boundaries instead of assuming REST performs defaulting
Do not import k8s.io/kubernetes direct package from staging; cross-path test belongs in root repository

experiments.title: Attribute managedFields and transform placement costs fairly
experiments.hypothesis: Part of measured direct-read allocation follows retained managedFields; trimming after conversion restores output shape without necessarily eliminating conversion allocations.
experiments.why: Current informer trims managedFields while direct retains it. Completed benchmark reports this mismatch; exact-output comparisons improve interpretation.
harness: Existing pkg/kubeapiserver/direct/read_cost_benchmark_test.go, first as a mechanism probe
Promote only qualified variants to N1's real storage harness
factors: ManagedFields payload 0/4082/32748 bytes; Get/List and existing populations
controls: All measured arms pass exact returned-field parity within their declared group
Pre/post source snapshots prove trimming only owned results
Include direct retained/output-trimmed comparison to locate savings rather than claim an end-to-end gain
observations: Allocations/op, bytes/op, CPU/time, raw and parity receipts
Separate fixture setup/update costs from reads
Payload-size slope and heap profile attribution
experiments.gate: No throughput/resource conclusion from mismatched outputs. A source mutation fails correctness. Do not propose a source-mutating early trim optimization.
caveats: Mechanism results remain component results until replayed through real cache
Output trimming after conversion may leave its deep-copy allocation cost

experiments.title: Production consumer route and readiness inventory
experiments.hypothesis: Actual production wiring leaves at least the node graph's Pod event consumer active in stage 1; context-aware and contextless routes differ by adapter.
experiments.why: Completed factory lifecycle test is narrower than all production consumer wiring. PR calls itself stage 1 of 2, so residual Pod watch is a boundary, not an unexpected author claim.
harness: Production initialization/adapters for NodeRestriction, PSA, ResourceClaim quota, token getter, node graph event registration
Existing lifecycle_contract_test.go and context_route_test.go as evaluator controls
factors: Consumer enabled/disabled with necessary dependent informers kept active
Pod lister reads only vs required Pod event consumer present
controls: Positive Pod event consumer demonstrably receives one bounded fixture update
No-consumer arm must have zero Pod List/Watch starts
Namespace/device-class/node and other resource readiness remain independently observed
observations: Actual Pod List/Watch, direct Get/List and fallback-client counts
PSA ListPods cancellation/deadline observed at its consumed adapter
Informer start, handler synchronization and stop receipts; record relevant gates
experiments.gate: BLOCKED if initialization prerequisites are changed to produce the desired route. Scope node graph checks to registration/lifecycle/event counts, not authorization outcomes.
caveats: PSA namespace readiness is separate from Pod cache readiness
Fake reflector may fall back from WatchList; register actual negotiated route
Any adapter experiment needs the production-consumed method, not an otherwise unused context-aware extension

experiments.title: Net update/read resource experiment with residual event consumer
experiments.hypothesis: Direct lister benefit depends on whether it eliminates informer update processing; with the event consumer retained it can add per-read conversion while much update work remains.
experiments.why: Issue142223 motivates update/relist allocations. Warm read-only microbench cannot establish total-system savings.
harness: Begin with real client-go informer plus qualified isolated cache-backed direct path from N1/N3
Then one isolated API server process per trial for end-to-end totals; state whether process totals include etcd and clients
factors: Lister cached/direct x Pod event consumer absent/present
Read-only, update-only, then mixed workload with fixed successful operation counts
Fixed object population and separately varied managedFields shape
controls: Exact read values and successful bounded update counts
Informer/event counts prove what actually disappeared
Update-only phase qualifies propagation and memory accounting; matched no-op receipt checks runner overhead
observations: Allocation bytes/second and per successful update/read
Retained heap after a declared GC protocol, CPU, GC pause and propagation lag
Total operation outcomes, watch/relist counts, goroutines and transport bytes
Phase times and setup/teardown separately
experiments.gate: Preregister improvement threshold and paired/factorial analysis before measurement. If a residual informer remains, report measured stage-1 net result rather than extrapolate stage-2 elimination.
caveats: Do not attribute umbrella issue's combined optimization QPS result to direct listers
Physical fake watch injection establishes mechanism only; a real-server trial must measure transport/update path

experiments.title: Bounded watch recovery and A1/B/A2 refinement
experiments.hypothesis: Removing redundant informer work changes relist/recovery costs only when that work actually exists; a short watch restart may resume without a full relist.
experiments.why: Issue142223 already has A1/burst/A2 proposal, so this refines and isolates it rather than claims a new idea.
harness: Qualified isolated server and event consumer from N3/N4
One controlled watch restart or bounded List error in a test transport; then a modest registered workload step
factors: Watch restart versus proven full relist
controls: Counters distinguish resumed watch from full List
No-event-consumer arm verifies absence of an informer recovery mechanism
A1 without perturbation establishes ordinary timing/resource variability
observations: Requested RV, actual List/Watch route/status, event gap and UID/RV catch-up barrier
A1/B/A2 latency/outcomes, allocation peak/area, GC/CPU and recovery duration
Explicit relist size, WatchList fallback and residual consumer counts
experiments.gate: Do not call an event a relist without receipts. Fix recovery tolerance, window and perturbation size before execution; evaluator failing to observe perturbation is BLOCKED.
caveats: Use small bounded fixtures and isolated test processes; no load on third-party clusters
Original issue's proposed recovery within 10% is a proposal; threshold must be calibrated and preregistered, not selected after results

experiments.title: Startup, catch-up and benign error/fallback contracts
experiments.hypothesis: Storage registration, cache readiness and informer synchronization produce distinct benign outcomes; exact fallback calls reveal extra reads hidden behind successful results.
experiments.why: Warm synchronized tests hide startup and fallback paths. CacheDelegator Get and GetList have different unready behavior.
harness: Own cache constructor for pre-ready trials: current Cacher test helper waits via cacher.Wait(ctx)
pkg/kubeapiserver/direct/factory.go / client.go and actual Pod REST/CacheDelegator
pkg/controller/serviceaccount/tokengetter.go:GetPod tested only as a benign object getter with counting client
factors: Before storage registration, before cache ready, after cache ready, after informer sync
Absent object; ordinary create/update/delete/recreate with UID/RV barriers
Live/cancelled/expired context on methods that actually accept it
Successful lister result versus benign NotFound/unready/error causing fallback
controls: Known object after synchronization must return registered identity
observations: Error type/status and returned UID/RV
CacheDelegator and backend route, handler-ready state and bounded cancellation completion
Number and timing of lister and fallback-client calls
experiments.gate: Do not demand equality before synchronization where contracts permit staleness. Register acceptable outcomes per readiness stage. Exclude token validation/authorization decisions.
caveats: CacheDelegator.Get with unready cache delegates to underlying storage even with RV0
GetList delegation depends on List options; otherwise Cacher readiness may yield TooManyRequests
Do not assume the startup outcome from Cacher alone describes its delegator

recommended_first_sequence: N4 update-only then mixed net resources
N5 bounded recovery after counters qualify
unresolved_dependencies: Locate compatible etcd executable and record its hash/version before real-storage execution
Commit exact new harness and frozen preregistration before collecting new results
Broader architectural direction remains pending the user's other model
